{
  "feasibility": {

    "answerable": [
      "Vertical soil moisture, infiltration, recharge, and column-scale water balance at representative hillslope positions using ELM's hillslope hydrology configuration (upland, mid-slope, toe, riparian) with prescribed downslope lateral connectivity",
      "First-order estimates of hillslope-to-stream drainage timescales from ELM subsurface lateral drainage plus PFLOTRAN saturated-zone flow within a single hillslope transect",

    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "True 3D lateral flow convergence across a real Naches DEM flow network (single-column/1D-transect ELM cannot resolve 2D planform convergence)",

      "Explicit particle-tracked travel-time distributions across the full catchment (needs a distributed routing/transport model beyond single-column ELM)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "ELM hillslope hydrology discretizes one representative topographic flowpath into ordered columns with downslope lateral connectivity. Four columns (upland, mid-slope, toe-slope, riparian) capture convergence and water-table gradients along the flowpath while keeping the single-hillslope PFLOTRAN coupling tractable; groundwater exchange is resolved between these adjacent positions but not between separate hillslopes.",
  "columns": [

    {"id": "naches_midslope", "lat": 46.900, "lon": -121.038, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_toeslope", "lat": 46.896, "lon": -121.031, "soil_texture": "loam"},

      "QLATERAL",

  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM hillslope hydrology (use_hillslope) with multi-column downslope lateral routing",
    "ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for saturated-zone lateral groundwater flow and inter-column exchange along the transect",
    "GSWP3 or site-adjusted DATM forcing for the Naches basin",
    "High-resolution DEM-derived hillslope geomorphic parameters (column distance, elevation, slope, width) to define flowpath connectivity"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single representative convergent hillslope transect in the upper Naches (near Bumping/American River divide, ~46.9N) stands in for basin behavior; results are transect-scale, not full-catchment",
    "Downslope lateral connectivity is prescribed by hillslope geomorphic parameters rather than solved on a 2D grid",
    "20-year spin-up-inclusive run (repeat/AD spin-up applied separately) is sufficient to equilibrate water table before analysis",
    "Travel times are inferred diagnostically from steady-state QLATERAL/QDRAI fluxes and storage, not from an explicit tracer/particle model",
    "Groundwater exchange is limited to the four connected within-hillslope positions; neighboring separate hillslopes are not represented"
  ]

answerable: Vertical soil moisture, infiltration, recharge, and column-scale water balance at representative hillslope positions using ELM's hillslope hydrology configuration (upland, mid-slope, toe, riparian) with prescribed downslope lateral connectivity
First-order estimates of hillslope-to-stream drainage timescales from ELM subsurface lateral drainage plus PFLOTRAN saturated-zone flow within a single hillslope transect
Groundwater table dynamics and saturated lateral flux along a single topographic flowpath via ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling
not_answerable: True 3D lateral flow convergence across a real Naches DEM flow network (single-column/1D-transect ELM cannot resolve 2D planform convergence)
Groundwater exchange between physically distinct neighboring hillslopes (inter-hillslope subsurface fluxes) — requires a distributed/3D domain, not a single-column campaign
Explicit particle-tracked travel-time distributions across the full catchment (needs a distributed routing/transport model beyond single-column ELM)

parsed.n_justification: ELM hillslope hydrology discretizes one representative topographic flowpath into ordered columns with downslope lateral connectivity. Four columns (upland, mid-slope, toe-slope, riparian) capture convergence and water-table gradients along the flowpath while keeping the single-hillslope PFLOTRAN coupling tractable; groundwater exchange is resolved between these adjacent positions but not between separate hillslopes.
requires_capabilities: ELM hillslope hydrology (use_hillslope) with multi-column downslope lateral routing
ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for saturated-zone lateral groundwater flow and inter-column exchange along the transect
GSWP3 or site-adjusted DATM forcing for the Naches basin
High-resolution DEM-derived hillslope geomorphic parameters (column distance, elevation, slope, width) to define flowpath connectivity
assumptions: A single representative convergent hillslope transect in the upper Naches (near Bumping/American River divide, ~46.9N) stands in for basin behavior; results are transect-scale, not full-catchment
Downslope lateral connectivity is prescribed by hillslope geomorphic parameters rather than solved on a 2D grid
20-year spin-up-inclusive run (repeat/AD spin-up applied separately) is sufficient to equilibrate water table before analysis
Travel times are inferred diagnostically from steady-state QLATERAL/QDRAI fluxes and storage, not from an explicit tracer/particle model
Groundwater exchange is limited to the four connected within-hillslope positions; neighboring separate hillslopes are not represented
